text: Not all men, but always a man. And in the caption it says, even as a statue, women cannot get peace. There is just one tiny problem. This is the statue of Juliet in Verona, Italy. Yes, from Romeo and Juliet, written by Shakespeare. And touching Juliet's right breast is literally a tourist tradition. People do it because it is believed to bring good luck in love. Even the official Visit Verona page has that information. And here's the slightly inconvenient part for the whole always a man narrative. Women do it too. A lot. It takes about 10 seconds of searching online to find hundreds of photos of women doing exactly the same thing. So this video was edited to show men participating in the tradition while leaving out women doing exactly the same thing. And with what purpose in mind? I think we all know the answer. To hate on men. To vilify us. To show how disgusting men are. And then the author also wrote, just something to think about, especially when we travel. How conscious we are of feminism and the roots of such cultural people, places, and things. And of course, the comments are full of support for her. Fortunately, there are some rational thoughts there too. One lady actually made what I think is the most important point. She wrote, That statue gets touched by women too, because people believe it brings good luck. That said, it is undeniably distasteful. But honestly, this is exactly the kind of content that makes people think feminism is obsessed with meaningless stuff. And it only fuels backlash. If you want to fight for feminism, do it right. We have plenty of real cases to bring to the table. Not manufactured scenarios carefully edited just to farm likes. Content like this only ends up hurting the cause. Bravo! This is spoken like a true feminist. And I completely agree. There are actual serious problems affecting women in this world. Including problems in Western countries, but especially in many other parts of the world. You don't need to manufacture examples. Because when you take something completely ordinary, selectively show men doing it, live out women doing exactly the same thing, and then present it as evidence of how terrible men are, you are not helping anyone. You are just giving people another reason to dismiss feminism when it talks about something that actually matters. And the saddest part is the replies this lady received. Oh honey, please start working on your internalized misogyny. Girl, go read and study. You are not a cool girl. You are wrong. You don't get paid to be a pick me. Even some guy wrote such a pick me comment. If you start thinking like this, you'll never fight for anything because there's always something worse. If you don't see that, you are part of the problem. She is not part of the problem. This woman and her attitude could actually be part of the solution. Because she seems to have the genuine spirit of a feminist, unlike the author of the post and the people who wrote those replies.
